title: Telemetry taper and release rhythm notebook (April 2026) - draft
body:
Purpose and scope:

This notebook defines a compact release rhythm for medium-impact rollouts (model variant swaps, config surface changes, infra-side batching updates) with an explicit telemetry taper plan to reduce false-positive alerts during expected transient spikes. It contains the preflight checklist, a deployment-day timeline, telemetry taper instructions, rollback/mitigation criteria, a sample rollout calendar for the next three weeks, and a draft of release notes to feed into product and support channels.

Objectives:
- Ship changes with predictable SLO exposure (target: <= 5% latency p95 increase, < 3% availability impact)
- Reduce noisy alerts during rollout by coordinating temporary signal dampening and traffic sampling
- Provide clear ownerable checkpoints so SRE, Release Eng, and Product know "go/no-go" signals

Quick summary of the change set:
- Serve runtime: enable continuous-batching heuristics for small-seq workloads (config flag: runtime.batch_small_seq=true)
- Routing: add new model-variant tag (v2-q4) with quantization-tweak profile
- Observability: add new caching KV metric (kv.cache_hit_ratio) and a KV cache warmup job

Preflight checklist (to be completed 72/24/2 hours out):
- 72h out (owners: Release Eng + SRE):
  - [ ] Confirm canary capacity (min 10% traffic to canary pool, 4 GPUs)
  - [ ] Validate model-variant compatibility matrix (ML lead sign-off)
  - [ ] Run synthetic throughput test at target QPS for 30m and capture p50/p95/p99
  - [ ] Draft release notes (PR to product channel)
  - [ ] Update runbook with rollback commands (included below)
- 24h out (owners: Release Eng + Observability):
  - [ ] Instrument KV cache metrics and make dashboards (Latency, Errors, kv.cache_hit_ratio, kv.warmup_progress)
  - [ ] Create smoke-test set and publish to staging (link in linked artifacts)
  - [ ] Schedule deployment window and on-call rotations (see roster)
- 2h out (owners: deployment lead):
  - [ ] Final infra health check (no active Sev>1 incidents for 2h)
  - [ ] Confirm rollback image is promoted and available in artifact registry
  - [ ] Notify stakeholders on #release-ops and update Zoom link

Deployment day timeline (UTC) - target: 2026-04-16
- T-60m: Final sync with dispatch channel (Release lead, SRE, ML lead, oncall)
- T-30m: Run quick smoke in staging and verify smoke runbook (5 green tests)
- T-15m: Lock non-essential merges and announce maintenance window
- T=0m: Start canary rollout (route 5% traffic to v2-q4 in us-west1)
- T+10m: Verify canary health (p95 latency delta, kv.cache_hit_ratio, 1% error threshold)
- T+30m: If stable, increase to 25% and start cache warmup job for hot prefixes
- T+60m: If stable, increase to 60% and keep monitoring; final promote to 100% no sooner than T+120m
- T+120m: Full traffic (if stable) and begin telemetry taper reversal schedule

Telemetry taper plan (why and how):
Rationale: When rolling out changes that alter batching/caching, raw metrics can spike briefly due to cold caches, transient queueing, and autoscaler activity. Tapering reduces alert thrash while preserving signal for real regressions.

Stepwise taper instructions (observability owner executes):
- Before T=0: duplicate primary alert policies (prefix: TMP-ROLLTAPER-) and set a temporary delay window + higher thresholds (examples below). Keep originals intact to restore later.
- T+0 to T+30m: Apply "mild taper" to latency-based alerts: p95 threshold +20%, increase evaluation window to 10m, require 2 evals. Reduce sampling of low-value traces by 50% (trace-sampler config).
- T+30 to T+120m: If canary shows healthy trends, keep taper but progressively reduce thresholds back (p95 threshold +10%). Turn on cache warmup dashboards and monitor kv.cache_hit_ratio rising trend.
- T+120m onward: Restore original alert policies and sampling rates in controlled steps (30m increments). Remove TMP-ROLLTAPER- policies.

Example temporary alert modifications (concrete):
- original: latency-p95-service > 220ms over 5m -> page
- temp: latency-p95-service > 264ms over 10m AND consecutive 2 evals -> page
- original: cpu-util > 85% 3m -> page
- temp: cpu-util > 92% 6m -> page

Rollback criteria (explicit):
- Immediate rollback (flip to previous image): any sustained increase in 5m error rate > 2x baseline AND absolute error rate > 1% for 10m
- Soft pause (hold at a previous traffic percentage and re-evaluate): p95 latency > target + 25% OR kv.cache_hit_ratio not trending up after 60m
- Manual rollback triggers: direct page from SRE lead or product owner citing business impact

Post-release validation (T+2h, T+24h, T+72h checks):
- T+2h (release owner): verify basic health (errors, latency, key business transactions). Publish a short status note to #release-ops.
- T+24h (SRE): run automated nightly smoke with longer-tail scenarios (batch sequences > 1024 tokens). Collect regressions and tag incidents.
- T+72h (ML+Product): evaluate quality metrics on a curated prompt set (sample size >= 5k calls). If quality drift > 3 points on the chosen metric, open follow-up ticket in REL-1420.

Release calendar (three-week cadence example) - high level:
- Week 0 (now -> apr-16): Stabilize, preflight, synthetic tests, docs and release note draft
- Week 1 (apr-16 -> apr-23): Canary rollout and early validation window; if stable, promote; otherwise, roll forward to hotfix cycle
- Week 2 (apr-24 -> may-1): Observability harden, revert taper fully, clean up TMP-ROLLTAPER policies, retro notes and runbook updates

Draft release notes (to be polished for product):
- Title: runtime: small-sequence continuous-batching and v2-q4 model-variant rollout
- Summary: Introduces a low-latency batching optimization for short sequence requests and a new quantization variant (v2-q4) aiming to reduce per-token cost by ~18% for small sequences.
- Notable changes:
  - Continuous-batching enabled for small-sequence requests (heuristic threshold: <= 64 tokens)
  - New model variant v2-q4 available; opt-in via model tag
  - KV cache telemetry added (kv.cache_hit_ratio) and warmup job
- Impact: Expected latency improvement for small sequences; brief transient variance possible during rollout while caches warm
- Action for customers: opt in to v2-q4 in model routing rules, contact support if you see sustained increases in error rates
- Known issues (targets for follow-up):
  - Some older SDK versions may not expose the model-variant header correctly (tracking: REL-1434)
  - Rare with specific prefix patterns, warmup may not reach desired hit ratio in 30 minutes (mitigation: extend warmup window)

Communication plan and stakeholder updates:
- Channel: #release-ops (primary), #eng-release (secondary), email digest to affected customers if promote to 100%
- T-60m: preliminary notice to #release-ops
- T+1h: status update (canary health summary)
- T+24h: short technical post with monitoring graphs attached

On-call roster (deployment window coverage) - keep short and clear:
- Deployment lead: Aisha Patel (release-eng)
- SRE primary: Marco Li (pager)
- Observability: Ethan Kim (dashboards + taper execution)
- ML lead: Priya Desai (model sign-off)
- Escalation: Head of SRE (on-call phone number in runbook)

Runbook snippet - quick rollback commands (examples):
- promote previous image: 
  - docker tag gcr.io/redwood/runtime:prod-2026-04-08-prev -> prod:latest && kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-service -n prod
- route traffic back to baseline: 
  - rtrctl traffic set service/runtime --weight 100 --variant baseline

Postmortem and retro template (if incident):
- Timeline: record every operator action with UTC timestamps
- Signal catalogue: include metric snapshots 30m pre-change, at T+0, T+30, T+60, T+120
- Root cause rubric: config/mismatch, infra capacity, model-quality, code regression, observability gap

Open questions & follow-ups:
- Should we make the taper automation a productized toggle in the alerting infra (EP for Q3)?
- Confirm SDK compatibility window for model-variant header (owners: DevX + SDK)
- Post-deploy: map any customer support threads to REL-1440 for tracking

Attachments and artefacts (links):
- Synthetic test results: s3://redwood-test-results/runtime/2026-04-08/small-seq-report.csv
- Canary dashboard (draft): https://grafana.redwood.local/d/runtime-canary-weekly
- Draft release note PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/156

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep taper windows conservative for the first two runs, we can shorten after one clean deploy
- Remember to rehydrate the sample tracer after step-up; sometimes traces drop off when sampling is changed
- Make sure product has an editable paragraph for customer-facing release notes (avoid technical jargon)

End of notebook.

(Will iterate after Monday's preflight sync; please add comments inline or ping on #release-ops.)
